claims.claim: The b/c > k cooperation criterion is derived for specific graph and weak-selection updating conditions, not arbitrary games or topologies.
claims.locator: Ohtsuki et al. (2006), assumptions for a simple rule and graph updating

claims.claim: The one-round donation-game payoff equals benefit from cooperative neighbors minus per-neighbor cost paid by cooperators under the explicitly specified interaction convention.
claims.locator: Original article and donation-game benefit-cost convention; teaching formula derived

claims.claim: In the voter model, a randomly selected node copies a neighbor's binary state according to a specified update rule, without consulting donation-game payoffs.
claims.locator: Holley and Liggett (1975), Voter Model; present example is a finite asynchronous pull variant

claims.claim: Hegselmann–Krause bounded-confidence dynamics average opinions among agents within a confidence radius.
claims.locator: Hegselmann and Krause (2002), continuous opinions and confidence radius

claims.claim: The four-node path with states 1,1,0,0 and donation benefit 3, cost 1 yields payoffs 2,1,3,0.
claims.locator: Derived from explicit per-edge donation payoff formula and executable oracle

claims.claim: For opinions 0.1,0.2,0.9 and inclusive confidence epsilon 0.2, one synchronous update gives 0.15,0.15,0.9.
claims.locator: Derived from specified self-inclusive uniform averaging update
